hints: Think about what happens to electron shells and electron repulsion when an atom loses electrons versus when it gains electrons.
Magnesium loses its two 3s electrons to form $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, leaving only the n=2 shell, so the cation must be much smaller than the atom.
Sulfur gains two electrons to fill its outer shell as $\text{S}^{2-}$, so increased repulsion with the same nuclear charge makes the anion expand beyond the atom.
walkthrough:
**Recall the cation rule**

Think of a metal losing electrons. You lose an outer shell and the remaining electrons are pulled in more strongly.

$$\text{Mg} \; ([\text{Ne}]3s^2) \rightarrow \text{Mg}^{2+} \; ([\text{Ne}]) + 2e^-$$

**Apply to magnesium**

Magnesium loses its whole n=3 shell. Fewer shells plus the same 12 protons pulling on only 10 electrons means a big contraction.

$$\text{Mg} > \text{Mg}^{2+}$$

**Recall the anion rule**

Think of a non-metal gaining electrons. The number of shells stays the same, but extra repulsion spreads the cloud out.

$$\text{S} \; ([\text{Ne}]3s^23p^4) + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{S}^{2-} \; ([\text{Ar}])$$

**Apply to sulfur and conclude**

Sulfur keeps 3 shells, but 16 protons must now hold 18 electrons, so repulsion wins and the ion swells.

$$\text{S} < \text{S}^{2-}$$

options.A: The magnesium part is correct, $\text{Mg} > \text{Mg}^{2+}$, but the sulfur part is wrong. Anions are larger than their parent atoms, not smaller, so $\text{S} > \text{S}^{2-}$ cannot be true.
options.B: This is correct. Cations shrink because an outer shell is lost and effective attraction increases, so $\text{Mg} > \text{Mg}^{2+}$. Anions expand because added electrons increase repulsion with no extra shell change, so $\text{S} < \text{S}^{2-}$.
options.C: Both parts are reversed. Students choosing this think losing electrons makes things bigger and gaining electrons makes things smaller, which is the opposite of the shell and repulsion logic.
options.D: The sulfur part is correct, $\text{S} < \text{S}^{2-}$, but the magnesium part is wrong. $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ has lost the n=3 shell, so it must be smaller than $\text{Mg}$, not larger.
